head: claude/drain-ml-backlog-pass2
title: ml-backlog drain #3: the no-exit class is 10 mislocated exit conditions, not 10 missing ones (22 examined / 0 closed / 22 refused / 1 filed)
body:
## Denominator at base sha `68e73de8`

Verified independently at my base rather than inherited: **106 rows — 84 `resolved`, 19 `kept_open`, 3 `open` = 22 unresolved.** Matches the brief. The ratio is the shape: `kept_open` outnumbers `open` 6×.

`main` at `68e73de8` already carries #10724 (health drain #2) and #10725 (research drain #2).

## Burn-down

| | |
|---|--:|
| examined | **22** (every unresolved row) |
| **CLOSED** | **0** |
| REFUSED | **22** |
| FILED | **1** |

**Zero closures, and that is the honest outcome — no row's exit condition is satisfied.** Four of them I did not carry forward on assumption: I measured them and they came back unmet, which is below.

What did move is the **class**, measured on criterion 4's own predicate: the ml `kept_open` no-exit-condition census goes **10 → 0**, the first of the four backlogs to clear it. Corpus **36 → 26**.

## Reconciliation at head (`622cba7c`)

```
rows: 106 -> 107
  lost   : NONE
  added  : ['MB-20260902-SHADOW-ARCHIVES-SYNCED-SINCE-0816-AND-NO-READER-RESOLVES-THEM']
  status before: {'resolved': 84, 'kept_open': 19, 'open': 3}
  status after : {'resolved': 84, 'kept_open': 19, 'open': 4}
  unresolved: 22 -> 23      (22 examined, 0 closed, +1 filed => 23)
  rows whose status CHANGED: NONE
```

Asserted structurally, not by eyeball: id sets identical, non-`items` top-level keys identical, **0 pre-existing keys mutated, 0 keys lost, 0 rows lost**. The 9 removed lines in the raw diff are previous last-key lines gaining a trailing comma. Writer was `backlog_append.detect_format`, whose no-op round-trip on this file is byte-identical (651,171 → 651,171 bytes, `indent=2, ensure_ascii=False`) — so no reformat and no re-attribution.

## Was there a real class? Yes — and it is not the class the register says it is

`BL-20260825-KEPT-OPEN-ROWS-WITH-NO-EXIT-CONDITION-CAN-NEVER-BE-RETIRED` records that these rows *state no condition that would ever close them*, and its 2026-08-25 update generalises that the remainder "carry nothing to derive a criterion from, so giving them one would mean inventing an exit condition for a finding whose author did not state one".

**For this backlog that is measurably false. 10 of 10 authors DID state one.** Every no-exit ml row carries a falsifiable exit as **prose inside an `updates` entry** — nine of them literal `TRIGGER:` lines from the 2026-08-16 sysrev pass, one a `WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS:` block. `updates` is a history log, and no field-reading consumer looks there. So the exit conditions were never missing; they were **mislocated**, in a place the census, the guard and the work-object migration all structurally cannot see.

**What I did:** promoted each row's own condition into the field the repo's own convention prescribes — `trigger_condition` (353 corpus rows, 74 already in this file, documented in `docs/claude/model-refinement-lifecycle.md` as "the measurable thing that re-opens evaluation") where the author wrote `TRIGGER:`, and `resolution_criteria` where the author wrote `WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS`.

**The 9 promotions are provably verbatim, not paraphrased.** Extraction was programmatic and each result was asserted to be a substring of its own serialised row before being written; the script fails rather than writes otherwise. Each carries a stamp naming the source update's date and saying this session neither authored nor judged the condition.

The 10th (`MB-20260712-SHADOW-LOG-HISTORY`) I did **not** promote — its prose reads "enough shadow history to make the trade-vs-score join viable", which names no threshold and is exactly the "criterion nobody would ever check" the class row forbids. It got a criterion authored from *my own measurement* instead, which is the one case the brief permits.

⚠️ **This closes no row and is not claimed to.** The rows are exactly as open as before. What changed is that their exit conditions became machine-visible.

### Positive control

Metric and guard are one derivation (`scripts/ops/check_backlog_criteria.py`), so I exercised that derivation rather than a second one:

| run | ml census |
|---|--:|
| A baseline (this tree) | **0** |
| B strip one promoted field | **1** |
| C strip a second | **2** |
| D restore | **0** |

Restore byte-identical (`cmp -s` → YES). B alone could not distinguish "the census counts fields" from "the census is broken"; A-then-D is what makes the 0 trustworthy.

### ⚠️ And the number I am NOT allowed to quote alone

`check_backlog_criteria.py` contains **two different predicates** for "does this row have an exit condition", and they disagree:

* line 160, the `kept_open` census — accepts **any of 15** `EXIT_CONDITION_FIELDS`. → ml **0**.
* line 247, the per-row field check — requires **`resolution_criteria` specifically**. → ml **8 still lacking**.

A third consumer, `scripts/ops/migrate_backlog_to_work_objects.py:161`, also reads only `resolution_criteria`, so those 8 still produce a work object with a loud `⚠️ UNKNOWN` done-condition. **So: 1 of 3 consumers is satisfied, 2 are not.** I chose semantic honesty over the flattering number — a `TRIGGER:` is a re-open condition, and copying it into `resolution_criteria` would make a row read as closable when its trigger merely re-opens evaluation (and would leave two copies free to drift). The divergence is reported below, not papered over.

## Closures

**None.** Nothing to report under this heading.

## Refusals

All 22, with the reason. The four I *measured* rather than carried:

**1. `MB-20260717-M24-FUNDING-VISIBILITY` — REFUSED on measurement; its own conditional now resolves.**
The row had carried two open questions ("needs live data") since 2026-08-16. Population: `trade_journal.db::trades` via `GET /api/bot/db/table/trades`, read 2026-09-02T03:23–03:24Z; whole table n=5324; `bybit_2` subset n=1644, fetched **complete** across all pages with `filter_state == "applied"` asserted on every page.
* funding: `funding_paid_usd` is **null on 1644 of 1644** bybit_2 rows. Not zero-valued — never populated.
* broker cost: `cost_source='broker'` = **3** whole-table, and all 3 are bybit_2. `estimate` = 1473; `local_compute`/`exchange`/`none` = 0; 3848 null. Coverage **3/1476 graded rows = 0.20%**.
* ⚠️ The numerator has **not moved at all** since the row's 3/814 reading, while the bybit_2 denominator roughly doubled (814 → 1644). Static in absolute terms, going backwards as a ratio.

Controls, because a filtered count on this route is a documented trap: a nonexistent value → `total=0` with `applied` (so a 0 is a real 0); `estimate`=1473 (the probe finds positives); and a **bogus column → `total=5324` with `filter_state='ignored_unknown_column'`** — the whole table, reproducing live the exact `CLAUDE.md` hazard where an ignored filter reads as "matched every row". Every count was read only after asserting `applied`.

**The disposition advance:** the row says *"If (1) still reads 0, the fix is the DATA-VISIBILITY path (an operator Bybit UM funding export), not a puller code change."* (1) does still read 0. The row is therefore **operator-blocked, established by measurement**, and no puller code change should be proposed for it. That also keeps `MB-20260717-M24-NET-R` blocked, whose trigger is this same crossing.

**2. `MB-20260712-SHADOW-LOG-HISTORY` — REFUSED, and its current framing REFUTED.**
The 2026-08-29 triage calls it "a data-horizon limit, not a defect". It is a defect, and a located one.
* *The fix shipped.* The 2026-08-16 note says the archives are "NOT synced … four literal paths … with no glob". **Field beats comment:** at `68e73de8`, lines 335–358 carry a dedicated `shadow_predictions_archives` block globbing all four rotated forms, with an `archive_count` assertion and a three-state emit. `git log -S` dates it to `a620f2a8`, 2026-08-16 13:22:40 +0300 (#9612) — **the same session, ~4h after it wrote "blocked on a Tier-1 tooling change"**. The clone is shallow (586 commits, oldest 2026-08-14) but that date is *inside* the visible window, so it is a real read.
* *It is exercised.* `GET /api/bot/ml/db_pulls?limit=500`, read 2026-09-02T03:26Z, mirror 110s stale, window 2026-08-23T04:18Z → 2026-09-02T00:23Z, n=500 = the requested limit **so this is a tail, not the lifetime**. 60 rows = 30 `pulling` + 30 outcome; **all 30 `ok`**; `archives` = 2 on 29, **3 on the newest**. Negative control: the block's own `none` and `skipped` states never fire, so `ok` discriminates rather than defaulting.
* *And nothing reads them.* Denominator: **35 files** under `ml/`, `scripts/`, `src/` mention `shadow_predictions`; the only two touching a rotated form are its rotator and its puller. Every reader resolves one literal file (`ml/shadow/factory.py:85`, `ml/shadow/drift_retrain.py:128`). Positive controls: the archive pattern *does* find the puller (5 hits), and `.glob(`-using readers *do* exist under `ml/` + `scripts/ml/` + `scripts/research/` (6 files) — so the zero is real, not a broken probe.

Closing on the sync alone would be the "success true relative to its own scope, while the scope is wrong" failure `§ Green is not evidence` names. Split the located defect into its own row; this one keeps the symptom.

**3. `MB-20260721-MES-15M-HEAD-PARKED` — REFUSED; re-verified live.** `GET /api/bot/ml/registry`, 96 rows, mirror 86s stale, read 2026-09-02T03:19Z: `mes-regime-5m-lgbm-v2` is `LIVE`, `mes-regime-15m-lgbm-v2` still `SHADOW`. The whole LIVE bucket is 3, agreeing exactly with `/api/bot/ml/status` `registry.stages.advisory = 3` — two surfaces, same answer. Neither limb met; the head-to-head is trainer work. It is an operator decision either way.

**4. `MB-20260726-OI-HISTORY-LIMIT` — REFUSED; precondition recorded.** Same registry read: exactly 2 models carry `funding` in `model_id` — `btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-svble-v1` (SHADOW) and `btc-regime-1h-lgbm-funding-v1` (OFFLINE). Being *at* shadow is the precondition for "becomes a promotion candidate", not the event; establishing candidacy needs a powered gate-check on the trainer.

**The other 18** are refused on access or on tier, not on effort:
* **Trainer-VM-blocked (no HTTP diag API there; the `trainer-vm-diag` issue relay 403s for this session — a write-scope boundary, not the transient MCP drop):** `MB-20260719-PROMOREADY-OOSEDGE-OOM` (needs `/usr/bin/time -v` under `MemoryMax`), `MB-20260712-EXIT-ANALYSIS-COVERAGE` (shard inventory), `MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` (needs a v2 rebuild + re-audit), `MB-20260727-CONVICTION-AB-AUC`, `MB-20260704-T12-SSL-NEGATIVE`, `MB-20260705-META-LABEL-WALL`, `MB-20260705-FC-SLTP-GEOMETRY`, `MB-20260814-EXIT-HEAD-SCALP-SCOPING-IS-GEOMETRY-CONDITIONED`, `MB-20260618-XA-D2B`, `MB-20260723-M29-AI-SYSTEM-DYNAMICS`.
* **Already snoozed with a named trigger, correctly out of review passes:** `MB-20260613-002` (2026-11-01), `MB-20260627-003` (2026-09-30).
* **Dependency-chained on a row above:** `MB-20260717-M24-NET-R`, `MB-20260717-M23-META-LABEL`, `MB-20260717-M25-PROMO-CONSOLIDATE`.
* **Worked one hour earlier by ml-drain #1 (#10718) and correctly refused there; I did not re-do them:** `MB-20260822-ETH-15M-HEAD-IS-AT-CANDIDATE-NOT-SHADOW`, `MB-20260829-MES-1D-…`, `MB-20260829-MANIFESTS-DECLARE-COLUMNS-…`.

## Filed

**`MB-20260902-SHADOW-ARCHIVES-SYNCED-SINCE-0816-AND-NO-READER-RESOLVES-THEM`** — split out of refusal 2, carrying the located defect while the parent keeps the symptom. Filed through `backlog_append.py` (the similarity probe did not refuse; noting that its silence is token-overlap and not proof of novelty — I had already read the related rows). Its criterion explicitly rules out the two things that would falsely close it: `db_pulls` reporting `ok`, and a glob added to a reader nobody runs.

## One metadata correction

`MB-20260719-PROMOREADY-OOSEDGE-OOM` carried `tier: "T1"`, which the guard flags as unreadable. Rewritten to `"1 (T1 — offline trainer tooling; no order path)"`, preserving the original token verbatim inside the annotation. It was the only tier-unreadable row in this file. **The finding itself is untouched and not re-validated** — its criterion needs a trainer run.

## Verification

`scripts/ci/run_guards.py` on the **committed** tree: **PASS 34 · FAIL 0**, no uncommitted-work caveat. `pytest` was absent from this sandbox, which is the sole reason `artifact-validity-guard` and `operator-owed-guard` failed on a first run; I installed it (9.1.1) and re-ran, so both **genuinely executed** rather than shipping a caveat. No guard or test was weakened.

## Caveats — OBSERVED vs INFERRED

**OBSERVED** (measured this session; each with its population above)
* ml no-exit census 10 → 0; corpus 36 → 26; the A/B/C/D control.
* All 9 promoted strings are substrings of their own rows (asserted in-script).
* bybit_2: 1644/1644 null funding; `cost_source='broker'` = 3 whole-table; `estimate` = 1473; the `ignored_unknown_column` control returning 5324.
* `shadow_predictions_archives`: 30/30 `ok`, archives 2→3, zero `none`/`skipped`, over the stated 500-row tail.
* 35 files mention `shadow_predictions`; only the rotator and puller touch a rotated form.
* Registry: 96 rows, 3 LIVE, MES 15m still SHADOW; 2 funding heads (SHADOW/OFFLINE).
* `refusing_manifests_24h` = exactly 4, one of which is `setup-candidates-metalabel-xsym-yz-v1`.
* Manifest pins vs builder versions: `market_features` v001 vs `v12`; `setup_candidates` v001 vs `v2`; `account_context` v001 vs `v2`; `setup_labels` **v002 vs `v2`**.
* Guards PASS 34 / FAIL 0 on the committed tree with pytest present.

**INFERRED** (falsifiable — check these rather than inherit them)
* *That the mislocation is the general cause of this class.* Measured 10/10 **in this backlog only**. Health still shows 21 and performance 5; I did not open them, and their rows may genuinely carry nothing.
* *That promoting to `trigger_condition` is the right field.* It follows the repo's stated convention and the authors' own wording, but it satisfies 1 of 3 consumers — see the divergence above. A reasonable person could argue for duplicating into `resolution_criteria`.
* *That `a620f2a8` is the first commit introducing the archive glob.* `git log -S` on a **shallow** clone (deepened to 586 commits, oldest 2026-08-14). The commit is inside that window, but an earlier partial implementation would be invisible.
* *That nothing reads the archives.* A static-search negative with two positive controls. A consumer constructing the path dynamically would not be caught.

**NOT ESTABLISHED — refused rather than proxied**
* Anything requiring `dataset_audit.jsonl`, a trainer run, a dispatched workflow, or a new sweep. Missing access, named precisely: the trainer VM has no HTTP diag API, and `issue_write`/`add_issue_comment`/`create_pull_request` all 403 for this session (write-scope boundary — `curl` to `api.github.com` 403s at the proxy too, and retrying does not clear it).
* The 4 rows lacking `severity`. Deriving one would be **my** judgement, not the author's, and that is the invention this class exists to prevent. Reported, not filled.

## FOR THE MANAGER

**1. Criterion 2 of the no-exit class row — it is 7 rows, not 8, and the work is smaller than the criterion implies.**

The class row names 8 ml MILESTONE-PROGRAM rows to move to `ROADMAP.md`. Verified at `68e73de8`:

| row | status | milestone |
|---|---|---|
| `MB-20260717-M24-NET-R` | kept_open | M24 |
| `MB-20260717-M23-META-LABEL` | kept_open | M23 |
| `MB-20260717-M25-PROMO-CONSOLIDATE` | kept_open | M25 |
| `MB-20260717-M24-FUNDING-VISIBILITY` | kept_open | M24 |
| `MB-20260720-FCPCV-RETRAIN-NOOP` | **already `resolved`** | — |
| `MB-20260721-MES-15M-HEAD-PARKED` | kept_open | *(see below)* |
| `MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` | kept_open | *(see below)* |
| `MB-20260727-CONVICTION-AB-AUC` | kept_open | M16 |

* ⚠️ **`MB-20260720-FCPCV-RETRAIN-NOOP` is already `resolved`** — acting on the list as written would chase a closed row.
* ⚠️ **It is a de-duplication, not an authoring job.** M16/M23/M24/M25/M29 **all already have full `ROADMAP.md` milestone-table entries** (lines 117/124/125/126/130; 14–20 mentions each). The backlog row is the *second* home the criterion warns about, so the move is "supersede the backlog row with a pointer", not "write a ROADMAP entry".
* ⚠️ **Two of the seven are miscategorised and should NOT go to ROADMAP.** `MB-20260721-MES-15M-HEAD-PARKED` is an operator **decision** (its own 2026-08-29 update says so: "this is an operator DECISION … not work"). `MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` is a **defect** — a manifest pinning a stale shard. Moving a defect to the roadmap loses it.

So the actionable set is **5 program rows**, and each needs a pointer rather than a new entry.

**2. A cross-row linkage worth more than either row — and evidence the register is not being read.**

`MB-20260726-XSYMYZ-RANGEVOL-DEAD` (filed **2026-07-26**) already names the mechanism that `MB-20260829-MANIFESTS-DECLARE-COLUMNS-…` called "the one genuinely puzzling instance" five weeks later, and that ml-drain #1 re-derived from scratch this morning: *the dataset was never rebuilt on the newer builder, so a manifest pinning an old `dataset.version` reads a stale shard with the narrower schema.* **Neither 2026-08-29 row points at it.** I verified the mechanism in-tree independently of drain #1 and cross-checked it on a *different* instrument (live `refusing_manifests_24h`, which returns exactly the same 4 manifests drain #1 found via registry `latest_run`).

⚠️ **One refinement to drain #1's framing, which said "every one pins a low version string while its builder has advanced":** that is 3 of 4. `setup-quality-lgbm-v2` pins `setup_labels` **v002** against `builder_version 'v2'`, which is not obviously behind. And the comparison is only suggestive in any case — `market_features.py:412-414` states in the builder's own words that `builder_version` *"is metadata-only (it does not gate dataset path resolution)"*, so the two are different namespaces and "behind" is not a defined relation. The safe statement is the measured one: **3 of the 4 refusing manifests pin `v001`; the fourth pins `v002`.**

**3. Two derivations of "has an exit condition" disagree, inside partly the same script.**

`check_backlog_criteria.py:160` (census) accepts any of 15 fields; `:247` (field check) requires `resolution_criteria`; `migrate_backlog_to_work_objects.py:161` also requires `resolution_criteria`. A row can pass one and fail the other — 8 ml rows are in exactly that state right now. **I did not file this**: it is guard/tooling infrastructure, not an ML defect, and filing it in the ml backlog would put it in the wrong home — the very failure item 1 is about. It belongs to whoever owns `BL-20260825-…`.

**4. A class I could name but not retire: "the remedy shipped and the row never learned."** Three measured members in this one file — `MB-20260712-SHADOW-LOG-HISTORY` (fix shipped 2026-08-16, row still says "blocked on a Tier-1 tooling change"), `MB-20260719-PROMOREADY-OOSEDGE-OOM` (its own record: #7721 reverted a flag, #7722 shipped the fix 13 minutes later, "deployed and inert for 24 days"), and `MB-20260721-MES-15M-HEAD-PARKED` (parked on a design question that was already answered in code). Retiring it needs something that reconciles a merged fix against the row that requested it — beyond a one-file scope, and I am flagging rather than attempting it.

## Process

Board `START` posted **before** the first substantive tool call, from a separate branch so the relay's result commit could not become this PR's head and zero its checks. Board tail proved by a short page (`perPage=12 page=164` → 7 items). This PR is a **DRAFT**; auto-merge not enabled; the manager owns the merge. I hold no merge slot.
